newsitem.title: INDIA: India gilt yields steady in dull trade, call quiet.
newsitem.headline: India gilt yields steady in dull trade, call quiet.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday little changed from the day's opening levels in moderate trade, dealers said. Call money was traded in the 5.75-6.25 percent range against the day's opening 5.50-6.25 percent, they said.
Liquidity with banks was good and call money was unlikely to change much for the rest of the fortnight, dealers said.

"Basically, the call money market seems to have shrunk," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "With the Reserve Bank of India reducing cash reserve requirements for banks, pressure for funds in call has eased substantially."
Cash reserve requirements have been cut by two percentage points since the beginning of calendar 1996.
Dealers said yields on government securities remained steady in thin trade on Monday.

"There has been little change from weekend levels," a dealers said. "Market participants remain cautious and are unprepared to take positions as they are uncertain over the movement of interest rates beyond two weeks."
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded at a yield of 13.05 percent while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock traded at 13.50 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said a certificate of deposit maturing in January 1997 was traded in the secondary market at 14 percent.
No trades were reported in commercial paper although corporates were showing interest in placing three-month paper at 13 percent. "There are no buyers at the moment," a dealer said.
Rates on intercorporate deposits were unchanged at 17.0-19.0 percent for top-rated borrowers, dealers said.
